\chapter{Seventeen to Twenty}
\label{ch:mr-seventeen-to-twenty}
\hlchaptermodality{58}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can count to twenty, and I can build nineteen the way Marathi does -- one less than twenty rather than nine and ten.}

Complete MR-R58-seventeen-to-twenty and count one to twenty, then take ekoNiis apart into ek plus uun plus viis.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[satrā]{\mr{सतरा} (satrā) — seventeen}

\label{lesson:MR-C58-satra}



\begin{quote}
Count from \textbf{\mr{एक}} to \textbf{\mr{सोळा}} and stop. The book has taken you no further than that.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{सतरा}}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{सतरा}} — \emph{satrā} — \textbf{17}
\end{quote}

Sanskrit \textbf{\mr{सप्तदश}} (\emph{saptadaśa}), \emph{seven-ten}. \textbf{\mr{सत}-} is the \textbf{\mr{सात}} of two chapters ago and \textbf{-\mr{रा}} is the ten. From here the pattern finishes itself.

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{satrā} — seventeen
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{terā chaudā pandhrā soḷā} — the run up to it, without looking
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{thoḍaṁ pāṇī} — a little water
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{kuṭhe?} — where?
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is seventeen in Marathi? (\textbf{\mr{सतरा}}.) Say the number before it, and the one before that.

Sources: \href{https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/\%E0\%A4\%B8\%E0\%A4\%A4\%E0\%A4\%B0\%E0\%A4\%BE}{Wiktionary: \mr{सतरा}}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[aṭhrā]{\mr{अठरा} (aṭhrā) — eighteen}

\label{lesson:MR-C58-athra}



\begin{quote}
Count from \textbf{\mr{एक}} to \textbf{\mr{सतरा}} and stop. The book has taken you no further than that.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{अठरा}}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{अठरा}} — \emph{aṭhrā} — \textbf{18}
\end{quote}

Sanskrit \textbf{\mr{अष्टादश}} (\emph{aṣṭādaśa}), \emph{eight-ten}. \textbf{\mr{अठ}-} is the \textbf{\mr{आठ}} you met in chapter fifty-five, retroflex and all, and \textbf{-\mr{रा}} is the ten for the last time: nineteen is built a completely different way.

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aṭhrā} — eighteen
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chaudā pandhrā soḷā satrā} — the run up to it, without looking
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{puresaṁ} — enough
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{kadhī?} — when?
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is eighteen in Marathi? (\textbf{\mr{अठरा}}.) Say the number before it, and the one before that.

Sources: \href{https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/\%E0\%A4\%85\%E0\%A4\%A0\%E0\%A4\%B0\%E0\%A4\%BE}{Wiktionary: \mr{अठरा}}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[vīs]{\mr{वीस} (vīs) — twenty}

\label{lesson:MR-C58-vis}



\begin{quote}
Count \textbf{\mr{एक} \mr{दोन} \mr{तीन} \mr{चार} \mr{पाच}} and stop. Since chapter thirteen that has been the whole of what you can count.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{वीस}}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{वीस}} — \emph{vīs} — \textbf{20}
\end{quote}

Sanskrit \textbf{\mr{विंशति}} (\emph{viṁśati}) — the same word as Latin \emph{viginti} and, further along, English \emph{-ty}. It is the first number in this run that is not built out of ten and something else — and the next lesson will build \emph{nineteen} backwards from it, which is why it comes out of order.

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vīs} — twenty
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{soḷā satrā aṭhrā} — the run up to it, without looking
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{baraṁch} — quite a lot
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{the asking word in the answer's own slot}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is twenty in Marathi? (\textbf{\mr{वीस}}.) Say the number before it, and the one before that.

Sources: \href{https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/\%E0\%A4\%B5\%E0\%A5\%80\%E0\%A4\%B8}{Wiktionary: \mr{वीस}}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ekoṇīs]{\mr{एकोणीस} (ekoṇīs) — nineteen}

\label{lesson:MR-C58-ekonis}



\begin{quote}
Count from \textbf{\mr{एक}} to \textbf{\mr{अठरा}} and stop. The book has taken you no further than that.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{एकोणीस}}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{एकोणीस}} — \emph{ekoṇīs} — \textbf{19}
\end{quote}

This one breaks the pattern on purpose, and it is why \textbf{\mr{वीस}} came first: you cannot build nineteen until you have twenty. \textbf{\mr{एकोणीस}} is \textbf{\mr{एक}} (\emph{one}) plus \textbf{\mr{ऊन}} (\emph{less}) plus \textbf{\mr{वीस}} (\emph{twenty}): \textbf{one less than twenty}, counting DOWN from the round number rather than up from the ten.

Latin does the same thing with \emph{undeviginti}, and so does the clock face when somebody says \emph{quarter to}. Marathi uses this \textbf{\mr{एकोण}-} trick at every nineteen — twenty-nine, thirty-nine and the rest are all built this way — so learning it once buys every one of them.

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ekoṇīs} — nineteen
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pandhrā soḷā satrā aṭhrā vīs} — the run up to it, without looking
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{kitī sundar!} — how beautiful!
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is nineteen in Marathi? (\textbf{\mr{एकोणीस}}.) Say the number before it, and the one before that.

Sources: \href{https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/\%E0\%A4\%8F\%E0\%A4\%95\%E0\%A5\%8B\%E0\%A4\%A3\%E0\%A5\%80\%E0\%A4\%B8}{Wiktionary: \mr{एकोणीस}}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[satrā · aṭhrā · ekoṇīs · vīs]{The count reaches twenty, and the last step is taken backwards}

\label{lesson:MR-R58-seventeen-to-twenty}



\begin{quote}
Count from \textbf{\mr{एक}} to \textbf{\mr{वीस}} without stopping. That is fifteen numbers more than you had four chapters ago.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ek} … \emph{vīs} — the whole count
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ekoṇīs} and take it apart — \emph{ek} + \emph{ūn} + \emph{vīs}
  \item \emph{Say it:} which number in the run is NOT built out of ten — \emph{\textbf{\mr{वीस}}}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{\mr{थ}} — the aspirated dental
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
How is \textbf{\mr{एकोणीस}} built, and which direction does it count? (\emph{\textbf{\mr{एक}}} + \emph{\textbf{\mr{ऊन}}} + \emph{\textbf{\mr{वीस}}}; \textbf{downwards, from twenty}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
